name: Question 8
problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ to $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=-3{c}_{1}-5{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 6-5\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}6 & -5 \\ -5 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 5 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=-3{c}_{1}-5{c}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 5 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B={b1,b2} to C={c1,c2} is given below. Find [x]B given that x=−3c1−5c2.

PB→C=[4556]

a
[−36]
b
[−15]
c
[−98]
d
[−75]
e
[2−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

[x]B=PC→B[x]C.

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix PC→B from C to B. To do that, we compute the inverse of PB→C:

PC→B=PB→C−1=[4556]−1=14⋅6−5⋅5[6−5−54]=[−655−4]

Notice that since x=−3c1−5c2, we obtain [x]C=[−3−5].

Now, we compute [x]B:

[x]B=PC→B[x]C=[−655−4][−3−5]=[−75]
